thread:
Priya: FYI handing over primary for the KV memory-leak alert. paging still active for some customers in EU/US. full context below.

OpsBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv-store-high-mem (p99 mem usage > 92%) on prim-sec cluster eu-west-1 - triggered 12m ago. Incident ID INC-9453.

Priya: summary: we saw sustained tail memory growth on prim nodes after a customer spike. autoscaler tried to add pods but they OOM'd during warmup (~3x). fallback routing was engaged to secondary capacity which kept API success rate ~97% but p95 latency rose to ~1.8s for affected routes.

Samir: oncall notes: primary=Priya, secondary=Samir (I’ll be on standby for escalations). Handing until 0830 UTC. APAC night coverage gap from 00:00-06:00 UTC — make sure oncall-manager is aware.

Lena: Current mitigations in progress: 1) rolling restart of prim cache workers with reduced max-conns flag. 2) temp traffic-shed policy on heavy embeddings route (/v1/embeddings/bulk) to 20rps. 3) KV eviction threshold lowered to free headroom.

Priya: Commands I ran:
```
# restart fragile worker set
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/kv-cache-prim --field-manager=oncall
# reduce MaxConns for pool via feature flags
curl -X POST https://config.redwood.internal/flags -d '{"kv_max_conns": 150}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```

dylan: Observability: dashboards updated (link): https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/kv/INC-9453 - p99 mem for prim nodes shown. Also added a temporary alert for rapid heap-growth delta > 300MB/2m.

Samir: Customer impact: A subset of high-throughput customers saw 5-10% request timeouts during the initial spike window. No data loss reported. Support triage doc: https://confluence.redwood/INC-9453-customer-impact.

Priya: Playbook references used: runbook:kv-memory-leak.md (confluence) and the emergency-traffic-shape playbook. Key steps executed: lower eviction, restart workers one-at-a-time, engage secondary routing.

Lena: Temporary knobs we changed (monitor closely):
- kv.eviction_threshold -> 0.65
- embeddings.max_batch_size -> 512
- routing.secondary_weight -> increased to 0.35 for prim routes

Priya: Open tasks for next shift: 1) verify restarts finish cleanly (kubectl get pods -n inference | grep kv-cache-prim). 2) watch heap-delta alert for 30m. 3) confirm autoscaler scaling behavior after warmup tweak. 4) if OOMs continue, prepare to drain prim and cutover to secondary permanently (runbook step).

Samir: I'll own the watch window. If we see >2 OOMs in 20m on prim nodes, escalate to eng-runtime and trigger the draining play (see runbook link above).

Priya: Quick note on customer comms: support-sent an initial email to affected accounts, engineering draft is ready if needed. No public status page update yet; hold until we confirm full mitigation.

oncall-manager: Noted APAC gap — I’ll assign backup from rotations list (cc @Lena for overlap). Also please add a short blameless timeline to the incident doc while it's fresh.

Lena: small config diff I applied: `kv_config.yml` commit 7a3f9b1, pinned in incident doc.

Priya: handing over now. tagging logs + timeline in INC-9453. Samir — ping me if anything spikes. :thumbsup:

Samir: ack. I’ll do an initial check-in at +15m and update thread.

OpsBot: NOTE: scheduled follow-up check-in at 15m by Samir.

Samir: 15m update: restarts completed, no new OOMs observed in the last 15m, p95 latency trending down but still ~1.2s on embeddings route. continuing watch.

Priya: thanks, logging handoff complete.
